title: Historical depression candidate genes: large-sample preregistered null against candidate polymorphism and G×E hypotheses
summary: A negative-result record for the historical depression candidate-gene literature. Border et al. identified repeatedly studied candidate genes and tested polymorphism main effects, G×E effects, and gene-level effects in very large samples; the record preserves the null while avoiding anti-genetics overclaiming.

status_history.note: The seed identifies candidate-gene era psychiatric genetics as a major non-replication/negative-results subcorpus.
Promoted in rev0018 candidate-gene / GWAS denominator lane.

time.evidence_period: candidate-gene literature through large UK Biobank/PGC-era analyses; exact source periods require second pass

place.scope: psychiatric genetics / major depressive disorder candidate-gene evidence

subjects.name: historical depression candidate genes and candidate gene-by-environment hypotheses

claims.claim: Border et al. identified 18 depression candidate genes that had each been studied at least 10 times and examined candidate polymorphism main effects, polymorphism-by-environment interactions, and gene-level effects across large samples with Ns ranging from 62,138 to 443,264 across subsamples.
what_would_change_status: A corrected article/supplement changes the gene count, preregistration status, or sample-size ranges.

claims.claim: The study found no clear evidence for candidate polymorphism associations with depression phenotypes or polymorphism-by-environment moderator effects; as a set, depression candidate genes were no more associated with depression phenotypes than noncandidate genes.
what_would_change_status: A higher-powered or corrected analysis demonstrates robust effects for the same candidate polymorphism/main-effect or G×E hypotheses in the same scope.

claims.claim: The record is scope-limited: it does not say depression has no genetic component, or that GWAS proves causation; it says the historical large-effect candidate-gene hypotheses tested here were not supported, while GWAS remains a statistical-association method requiring biological follow-up.
what_would_change_status: A future review shows this scope caution is misleading or needs split by phenotype, ancestry, variant type, or G×E design.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass PDF/source extraction; supplement not locally hashed
limitations: Does not encode every candidate gene child record.
Does not resolve all depression genetic architecture questions.
Does not evaluate rare variants, polygenic scores, or non-European generalizability in detail.

type_payload.hypothesis_or_claim_tested: Historical depression candidate polymorphisms and candidate gene-by-environment interaction hypotheses had large detectable effects on depression phenotypes or stress-moderated depression risk.
type_payload.prior_evidentiary_route: Biological plausibility plus small candidate-gene studies, especially serotonergic hypotheses and 5-HTTLPR/SLC6A4 research.
type_payload.result_surface: large population-based and case-control samples with main-effect, interaction, and gene-level analyses
type_payload.field_correction_surface: GWAS-scale and consortium-scale testing made large common-variant candidate effects more falsifiable than earlier small candidate studies.
scope_cautions: Not a denial that stress is associated with depression.
Does not settle all possible rare-variant, polygenic, ancestry-specific, or phenotype-specific hypotheses.

handling_notes: Avoid stigmatizing psychiatric illness or implying genetic research is inherently suspect.
Treat early candidate work as historically understandable under prior genotyping costs and tools; the record concerns evidentiary status, not ridicule.
No individual participant or family-level genetic information is represented.

unknowns: Supplemental methods and exact preregistration artifacts not second-pass archived.
No child records for each of the 18 candidate genes.
next_actions: Add child records for SLC6A4/5-HTTLPR, BDNF, COMT, MAOA, DRD2/DRD4 if needed.
Pair with positive-control candidate-gene successes such as APOE/Alzheimer disease or alcohol-metabolism genes before maturing any pattern.
Source-acquire systematic reviews of depression genetics after 2019 for status-history updates.

scope_qualifiers.phenotype_scope: major depression / depression phenotypes in Border et al.; broad psychiatric trait caveat
scope_qualifiers.ancestry_or_population_scope: large biobank/PGC-era samples; ancestry composition requires second pass
scope_qualifiers.portability_caution: do not infer no genetic component or universal absence of GxE
